title: Strange Printer II
summary: The printer can only print a solid rectangular area of a single color at a time, and once a color is used, it cannot be used again.
statement: The printer can only print a solid rectangular area of a single color at a time, and once a color is used, it cannot be used again. Given an m x n matrix targetGrid where each element targetGrid[row][col] represents the color at position (row, col), determine if it is possible for the printer to produce the exact colors in the grid as specified.
constraints: Each color may be printed once as one solid rectangle, and later colors may overwrite it.
Return whether the target grid can be produced.
hints: Compute the bounding rectangle of every color.
A color can be the latest remaining print when every cell in its rectangle is itself or a color already removed from consideration.
Repeatedly remove all such colors; fail if a round removes none.
This is topological elimination of overwrite dependencies, so completing all colors is equivalent to a legal print order.
editorial: This is topological elimination of overwrite dependencies, so completing all colors is equivalent to a legal print order.

tests.explanation: Print the outer color-one rectangle first and overwrite its center with color two.
Each color’s bounding rectangle requires the other both before and after it, forming an impossible cycle.
